result.summary: This commercial street is characterized by an overhead rail structure that creates deep shadows and significant visual obstructions via large support pillars. While continuous sidewalks and active storefronts are present, the lack of marked pedestrian crossings and the physical encroachment of structural elements on the walkway reduce the overall safety and comfort of the environment.

hazards.name: Structural Pillars
hazards.description: Large steel columns for the elevated rail are located at the curb edge, creating blind spots for both drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the roadway at regular intervals

hazards.name: Lack of Crosswalks
hazards.description: No marked pedestrian crossings are visible in this active commercial area, increasing the risk of mid-block crossing conflicts.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install bold, continental-style crosswalks to clearly designate pedestrian crossing areas.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement bulb-outs at intersections to improve sightlines around the structural pillars and reduce crossing distances.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting fixtures beneath the elevated structure to improve visibility and security for pedestrians in shadowed areas.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a narrow sidewalk significantly obstructed by a large structural pillar and temporary metal barriers. The lack of a buffer between the walkway and the roadway, combined with blank frontages from closed roll-down gates, creates a somewhat confined walking experience.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large structural pillar for an elevated structure and metal barriers significantly narrow the usable sidewalk width.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: The large pillar blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening/Barrier Removal
interventions.description: Remove the temporary metal barriers to restore the full width of the sidewalk for pedestrian use.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility around the structural pillar.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting to the underside of the structure or on the pillar to improve visibility and perceived safety at night.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by an elevated rail structure whose support pillars create significant visual obstructions between motorists and people on the sidewalk. While continuous sidewalks and a painted bike lane are present, the lack of marked crossings and physical buffers from traffic reduces overall safety.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Large steel pillars for the elevated rail structure block the view between drivers and pedestrians, especially those attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the roadway at regular intervals

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible, which may lead to unpredictable mid-block pedestrian movements.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond the pillars and shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add zebra-striped crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian priority areas and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Upgrade the painted bike lane to a physically protected lane to provide a buffer between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

result.summary: This mid-block commercial environment is located under an elevated transit structure, which creates significant shadows and potential visibility issues. While a continuous sidewalk is present, it lacks a buffer from the adjacent travel lanes and is partially obstructed by temporary metal barriers.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: No physical buffer or dedicated parking lane exists to separate the sidewalk from active travel lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground

hazards.name: Reduced visibility from infrastructure
hazards.description: The elevated track structure and its support pillars create deep shadows and potential blind spots.
